CAPTIVĂ ÎNTRE PATRU BĂRBAȚI PERICULOȘI, O FEMEIE DĂ FRÂU LIBER CELOR MAI ASCUNSE DORINȚE.

Cei din clanul Viperelor controlează orașul în care trăiesc și pe toți locuitorii acestuia. Încheie înțelegeri la fel de sordide precum „afacerile” pe care le conduc. Și nu au pic de milă.

Fiindcă doar un idiot s-ar pune cu această familie de bandiți, evident că tatăl meu înstrăinat și abuziv s-a pus cu ei. Iar apoi m-a vândut Viperelor, ca să scape de datoria pe care o avea.

Da, m-a vândut!

Am devenit proprietatea lor.

Acum sunt prizonieră în penthouse-ul clanului, iar ei îmi repetă neîncetat că le aparțin întru totul. Însă Viperele nu știu cu cine au de-a face. Am de gând să profit de foamea care li se citește în ochi.

Pe măsură ce mâinile lor pline de cicatrici și mânjite de sânge îmi cutreieră corpul, eu le transform dorințele într-o dependență de care le va fi cu neputință să scape. Și, pe deasupra, voi savura cele mai întunecate fantezii, pe care nu am avut prilejul să mi le satisfac… până acum.

Ei îmi pot stăpâni trupul, dar nu și inima. Niciodată!

Voi avea grijă ca Viperele să regrete ziua în care m-au răpit.

Ryder, Garrett, Kenzo și Diesel au impresia că ei controlează totul.

Mă consideră prada lor. Dar și eu știu să mușc.

07/27/2023: Re-read via audiobook - DNF at chapter 5 - see bottom of review for comments

“Throw me to the wolves and I will come back leading the pack!”



This was a dirty filthy mafia story and it was very good. It was a long one though, it didn’t display pages but for how long it took me to read, I would guess at least 600-700 pages, though I could be wrong. But I would much rather read a long book like this than a series. I wish more authors would have one long book instead of three or four shorter ones. I can’t tell you how many times I have read a book and said I can’t wait to read book 2, but by the time it comes out I have either forgotten about it or am too busy to read the second book.

This was the story of Roxxane who is a tough as nails bar owner in the seedy part of town. Everybody in the area knows not to mess with her because she knows how to fight, she has a bat behind the bar that she is not afraid to use and she will fight dirty, with a kick to the cahone’s whenever possible.

When Roxy’s abusive father, whom she left when she was a teen, gets in debt to local mobsters called the Vipers he settles his debt by giving them his daughter. Then send four of their enforcers to pick her up and she gets the best of them. So the four Vipers come to her and take her as their captive.

What I liked about this book:

Roxy is an awesome heroine. She is independent, tough and beautiful. She isn’t afraid and she likes pain so she is able to stand up to the four hot as sin, tattooed tough guys that take her. They call each other brothers and all four are as close as real brothers because they have all been through hell and are broken in their own ways.



The leader is Ryder, he wears a suit and runs the Viper corporation, which is a legitimate company worth millions and has a lot of smaller companies underneath. Ryder is cold when he needs to be and his main goal is to keep his brother’s safe. Ryder’s real brother is Kenzo, who is more emotional but is also tough in his own way, he works with Ryder in the legitimate businesses. Kenzo also is a master at games and runs several illegal casino’s, he can also can throw down when needed.

Diesel is the assassin and his job is to torture and kill. He is a bit crazy from his childhood and loves to inflict pain, it is something he is very good at. Diesel can get anyone to talk when he gets to “play” with them. He is awesome and funny and cra-cra in a good way. He is the first to fall for Roxy.

Garrett is a tall muscular guy and he hates women and doesn’t like them being near him or touching him. He once fell in love and it went bad and he was betrayed, so he is determined not to make that mistake again no matter how much he wants Roxy. Garrett is the enforcer and he and Diesel make sure they are getting paid by those who owe them money and are in charge of the not so legal businesses. Though the vipers run the city and most of the cops are on their payroll. They can basically do what they want without fear.

I liked the storylines, first about the Roxy as a captive, then about their problems with the triad. I also really liked all of their background stories when each of them opened up about why they are broken and what their lives have been like. I also loved how hot and steamy the romances were. Though this is a reverse harem, it was generally like Roxy was having four separate romances. There was only one or two scenes where more than one of the were intimate with Roxy at the same time.

What I didn’t like about the book:

Though Roxy was awesome and very tough, I do think that there were a few times she was a bit too crass for me. Like one time she went with Ryker to a meeting with the board of Viper Corporation and she walks, sits down and puts her feet up on the table. I just don’t think that an adult who wants to be taken seriously would behave like that. She doesn’t need to curse at certain times and be disrespectful to look tough. I just think as a bar owner, she would know when to act crass and tough and when to act like a lady.

Another thing was that we know that Diesel is a bit crazy. He shows it in many ways but especially when he is getting information from someone in the basement of their building. We also know that Roxy likes pain and Diesel likes to cause pain so they do that when they are intimate. I just didn’t like that he said a few times, even after admitting he loved her, that he might kill her someday. He is so cute sometimes, with his crazy, but saying that was a bit too out there for me.

Though overall, I really liked this book. There were quite a few steamy scenes, but the book was very long so there was also a lot of story. I liked how it flowed and loved the action scenes. Roxy refers to John Wick a few times and this book does remind me of John Wick in a way because it was quite bloody and the bodies do pile up throughout the book. It is also hysterically funny at times and there were so many great quotes for me to put in my updates, that I couldn’t come close to using all that I wanted. I would say this was a 4 star review but the things I liked so outweighed the thing I don’t that it bumps it up to a 5. Especially considering that rather than a series, it is one long stand-alone book. I wish authors would do that a lot more.

The audiobook was told in multiple points of view via dual narration and was narrated by Hollie Jackson and Cornell Collins. I like Hollie Jackson for alien romance, but for this one she sounded a bit outside the right age range for Roxy, though she isn’t quite as bad as Cornell Collins. He sounds about sixty and his cockney accent for Diesel makes him sound like an old pirate and it made it hard to get into the story and hard to understand. Hollie also did a cockney accent which I hated. Between the two of them, it sounded like a Disney film where all the characters overacted to the extreme. I DNF’d the audiobook at about chapter 5 and I will re-read the print version sometime. I am not changing my rating, since the book was so good, but I DO NOT recommend the audiobook version.

Where do I even start with this mess of a book?

DNF @67%

TW: Kidnapping, Blood, Gore, Gun violence, Sexual Assault, rape, sexism, self harm, mental illness, death (on page), torture, toxic relationship, domestic abuse

To be fair, I knew I wouldn’t like this book, but I really did not expect it to be this bad. Right now, it has a 4.11/5 rating…it couldn’t be that bad, right?? Oh, I was wrong. I was so wrong.

Synopsis: After her estranged father sells her to settle a debt with the infamous band of brothers The Vipers, Roxy must work hard to stay safe or…lose her heart?

(Commence puking)

You Might Like This If
1. You enjoy dubious consent.
2. You enjoy reverse harem.
3. If you like smut, chances are this will be a satisfying read. The author is very good at building up tension before and during these scenes. Although, I must say that many of the scenes are extremely graphic. The pairing of violence and sex is a common theme within this book. If you like to explore those themes in conjunction with one another, this might be enjoyable for you.
4. You enjoy stories with multiple POVs.
5. You enjoy stories with unreliable narrators.

Ahem, now that that’s taken care of.

I HATE THIS BOOK.

I felt like I was in a freaking fever dream while reading this. Knight is truly an author to behold because somehow she managed to make me bored, angry, and just plain confused all at the same time.

Let’s introduce our cast of characters:
1. Ryder: he’s your everyday boss dude who thinks wearing suits is a personality trait. Toxic masculinity x100000.
2. Garrett: he’s our incel. He had a really traumatic experience with a woman and instead of fixing his shit and going to therapy, he has now turned to ~misogyny~
3. Diesel: I think his name explains it all. And while I don’t think an affinity for knife play means that you are a psychopath, he is definitely a psychopath. A murderous one at that. Weirdly enough, I think the author tries to use him as comedic relief.
4. Kenzo: my favorite. He is the gambler of the group. He’s definitely misogynistic and rape-y, but he’s the best of the group. That isn’t saying much.
5. Roxy: Annoying bitch with Stockholm syndrome who tries to convince you she doesn’t have Stockholm syndrome for 646 pages.

I don’t want to offend anyone, it’s okay to like what you like, but why the hell was this something people were recommending?? Out of all of the dark/taboo romances you could recommend, THIS is the one y’all are talking about 😭??

There are issues with this text, like, SERIOUS ISSUES. Lack of plot, pacing, very very problematic characterization of kidnapping and abuse victims. I feel like I must be missing something. I admit I am not a part of the BDSM community…but, idk, something tells me that Den of Vipers isn’t an accurate depiction of a healthy BDSM relationship at all.

But you know what it is an accurate depiction of? Stockholm syndrome.

This book tries its hardest to convince the reader that in some way Roxy CHOSE to stay with the Vipers. That she loves them. That this isn’t manipulative, at all. And that to me is disgusting. It also does its hardest to slut shame women, but I mean, what do I expect from a book that is literally depicting an abusive relationship with ZERO self awareness?

Here’s some quotes to enjoy (Possible triggering content: emotional abuse/manipulation, Sexual Assault)

"She doesn’t get to make Kenzo feel like he took her without consent. It would wreck him.”

🤡Are you kidding? It would hurt HIM?? YOU LITERALLY KIDNAPPED HER.

"She seems undisturbed by his rudeness, picking her nails with her new knife as she lounges. Why can’t she be this comfortable with us?”

Kidnapper wonders why kidnapee doesn’t treat him like a friend :/

"No deals, [Roxy], but know that tonight, I’m close to the edge. Plunge into that darkness, and you might not come back,” I warn.
She tilts her head…”Maybe I don’t want to.”

OMG i for real thought she was being suicidal here.

Listen, I think the last quote really speaks for the cheesiness and quality of writing, but I will just end on this.

“What if, without her, there is no us?
What if I can’t let her go?
What if I’m not strong enough?
What if I’m too much of a viper to release our prey?”

I am VIPER 🐍 ME NEED LADY 👿 or else...viper, no exist? 😪

This is existential for no FUCKING REASON

BYe.

Oh Lord.

I'm trying to discover more smut and romance in 2021 but I felt like this was 'not' the book I should have picked up to help me test those waters. I want to make it clear before I begin though that I do not want to kink-shame, especially since the sex scenes in this book are kinks I am not personally into. I do, however, find those scenes extremely unrealistic.

My reading vlog for this book has a lot of my more in-depth thoughts and live reactions to reading this book: https://youtu.be/NNF1dwa6y8E

Roxy is kidnapped after being sold by her father to the Vipers, four men who pretty much 'run the town'. They have a rivalry with the Triad that really doesn't inject that much excitement into the story. There's some attempt at a plot in this, but the flawed writing prevented me from remotely enjoying it.

I could not get on board with the romance from the very beginning due to Roxy being taken against her will and constantly abused and degraded. Yes, she does fall head over heels in love with them, and very early on (by around page 60) she even fantasises about them, but Roxy is painted on the blurb, and at the beginning of this book, as a woman who isn't pushed around by anyone. She's independent and fierce and WILL fight back against the Vipers to get her life back. Except... that doesn't happen! She allows them to sexually degrade her THROUGHOUT the book where her consent is taken away constantly. Her internal monologues enjoys it, apparently, but I don't understand her character at all. One minute, she wants to escape and get her life back, and the next, she is madly in love with her kidnappers?

The Vipers are all disgusting. There is some attempt at humanising them with backstories, but quite honestly, their penchant for murder and abuse, as well as the kidnapping and sexual assault of women, makes it *really* hard for me to care one little bit about them. They are irredeemable, and even at the very end, they remove Roxy's consent AGAIN and the writer tries to make it look like Roxy is a warrior? No, not in the slightest. This kind of storyline could have been handled with nuance and the topic of Stockholm syndrome could have been interesting to explore, but this is 'not' the book to take it seriously. The writer wants us to think one thing, but then think something entirely different in the next sentence - it's soooo confusing!

The sex scenes became so repetitive and boring. The same words were used over and over (and word choices were extremely cringe and downright horrific at times), that this book is overshadowed by the tediousness this book becomes by page 300 out of 600. Again, I do not want to kink-shame anyone, but I can't get my head around the logistics of some of these sex scenes - there's just no way some of them are possible without death / serious harm. Not only that, but the fact the Vipers are supposed to be big strong men, yet they last about 10 seconds in the bedroom. They're horny teenagers that can't stop thinking about abusing Roxy, or touching themselves.

I went into this hearing about the hype and my intrigue of it was very high, so it kept me reading, but I would not recommend this to anyone. I know my reading vlog has funny reactions to it, but if you aren't typically a reader of this kind of book, then steer well clear, or at least know the trigger warnings before going into it (sexual abuse, assault, violence).

I see now why this book is so popular. It’s my first book by KA Knight, but I’m impressed. She can write death and gore just as well as she can beautiful soul searing prose. Don’t even get me started on the hilarity, I don’t recall laughing out loud this much for a book. Wonderful really!

This is the first RH where all the dudes each have their very own personality. I know exactly whose chapter I’m reading because of fantastic character development. This one just keeps ticking all the boxes.

Can’t say I saw Roxxane coming but I like her a lot. Her and her bat.

Diesel may be in your face crazy but Kenzo is that low down, don’t know till it’s too late insane.

Girl, get it! Fuck Ryder! But the fact that she ran to Garrett, too funny.

Does anyone else find it amusing that she keeps talking to her girly bits?

Honestly the only interesting thing about Ryder is that she keeps fucking up his shit.

Tit for tat or should I say dick? Never gamble with a professional. 🤣 If that’s how it is with Kenzo I can’t even imagine what’ll happen with Diesel.

In all honesty I didn’t know if I was gonna like Diesel. But then the rhapsodizing about his past and how he wouldn’t change a thing because it brought him to his little bird ... well shit. How do you not fall in love with that?

Then he eats a piece of garlic bread and suddenly I don’t hate him anymore? The fuck?!

She doesn’t know her goddam birthday? Please tell me her sorry excuse for a father gets what’s coming to him. Hopefully at her hands.

I liked Kenzo from the get go, he’s probably my favorite. But after the cemetery? He has my heart.

The emotional moments are just so good. She has them with every guy and each one is beautiful in its own way. Now I can’t imagine why I ever hated Ryder, how I thought D was a one dimensional maniac, Garrett was a grump.

If you know me, you know I’m not a fan of captivity books. So even I’m asking myself, why do you like this? Good question and the answer is ... I have no idea. But I do know that situation was handled very well, in a way that made it work. She’s a bird after all.

You know what I love best about Ryder? From the outside looking in he appears useless because they’ve made him like the ‘face’ of the group. But in reality he can do everybody’s job better than they can. Jeez, if he’s not careful he’ll go from being my most hated to most loved.

The problem with this book is it’s too long and not enough plot. Also, I know it’s RH and expected, but too much sex. I enjoyed it more when they showed her their world than their cocks. Don’t get me wrong, I love that shit but I’d love it more if I had to work for it.

I can’t believe I’m saying this and I’m no doubt in the minority but Diesel isn’t one of my favorites. Yes, I love his character, I love how multifaceted he is, how funny and crazy and sweet. But as a boyfriend? Too fucking clingy! Sorry, not sorry. I’d pick one of the brothers or both.

I said it once but it bares saying again, this book is too goddam long. Those last two hundred pages dragged like a motherfucker. I would’ve gladly given this five stars if it wasn’t for that.

➽ KITTY KATS CRAZY ABOUT BOOKS

DEN OF VIPERS: Is a full length dark, reverse harem romance book by new to me author K.A. Knight. Various POV's.

One word ➤ PHENOMENAL! This was AMAZING As you know I like my grittier, edgier, darker non conventional books and this one right here ticked all my boxes. Like a tidal wave, I was pulled under by this authors spell as this book literally got its hooks into me from just that first page.

Get ready to meet your next addiction!! The Four Vipers and the one girl who wrapped them around her little finger. This on my ipad was over 1,000 pages long, so for me it took me over a day to read and devour.

If you like your heroines tough and sassy then you have to meet Roxy our bat welding girl who doesn’t go down without a fight. She owns and lives above her dive bar, which was gifted to her by the only man she ever cared about, no one messes with her, and anyone who is dumb enough meets her bat which is hidden behind her bar!! When Roxxane's estranged father who she ran away from in her late teens gets in over his head in a gambling debt with the Vipers the cities Mafia, he settles it by handing his daughter over to them.

Normally these guys don't deal with flesh but they have to show the city that they aren't going soft. This puts out a warning to anyone else who thinks about crossing them. When you fuck with Vipers, you get fangs.

Thinking it's one quick extraction they send in four of their top trustworthy enforcers to go to her dive bar and claim whats theirs. But Roxie doesn't give in without a fight, out comes that bat and she wipes the floor clean.



Enter the Vipers. These guys are the baddest motherf#ckers of the city, the untouchables, Everyone in the city respects them and everyone fears them, they are men you don't mess with.

The leader is suit wearing Ryder, he's the face and brains of their empire, he's calculating, and everything he does, he does it for his family, he's as dark and as cold as they come, a lethal business owner.

Kenzo is a charming psychopath he's also Ryder's brother, he runs the illegal casino’s they own, the groups bookie, he's the numbers guy, he's also a master at playing games.

Diesel (The Grim Reaper) he's bat sh#t crazy he's the assassin who comes up with unique ways to torture and kill their victims for shits and giggles. He's unpredictable, a predator, your worst nightmare. He'll send you to hell with a smile on his face. He burns in the flames of darkness. he's the very reason why the city is scared of the Vipers.

Garrett is our scarred big man fighter. The enforcer. He's the one that scares people until they are ready to talk to Ryder. He doesn't like to be touched and hates woman. He hates Roxx on sight but tough bickies because when the guys took her, she ended up in their apartment that they all share!!

🔥Holy hotness 🔥They could probably talk the panties off a nun. These guys were beyond hot!!

This was deliciously dark! My nerves were hanging on by a thread, like an adrenaline junky needing that next fix, my foot was tapping, my heart was out of beat, my hands were clammy, loving that electrical surge making me read faster. This book kept me on my toes throughout, the heat, the darkness, the grittiness quickly became my guilty pleasure.

I bloody adored this like massively, my First experience of this author and now I just want to binge-read all her backlist I was that impressed with this.

This is Dark Reverse-harem but it's the situations and actions of the characters involved that add the darkness to this one. The building relationships between Roxy and her men I actually found rather sweet and intense if majorly untraditional and intensively unique. Each of them brings something solely them to the table and together they are a family. A messed-up totally psychotic one but a solid loyal unit all the same.

The Vipers run and own the city so when Roxy's estranged father finds himself in their debt he pays his due in flesh with his daughter. Roxanne's background isn't exactly glamorous but what it's done is build the foundations of a strong take no bull individual. Now running a local dive-bar she's not afraid to get her hands dirty. A dynamo of silver hair, tattoos and piercings with a mouth on her that would make sailors blush. She's unpredictable, resilient and pragmatic she also isn't exactly thrilled to find herself the personal property of the Vipers.

The Vipers are the big-man about town nobody crosses them without paying in blood. Ryder is the face of the Vipers he is essentially their leader keeping the others in line both physically and emotionally. On the surface, he is Suited, calm, cold and collected with his fire locked down fire behind a wall of ice, still waters run deep with this one.
Ryder ultimately feels responsible for his fellow Vipers, he also needs control worried that he will become his father.

Kenzo controls the gaming halls and all gambling across the city he's Ryder's blood brother and the younger of the two. Ryder has always tried to protect Kenzo who's much more in touch with his emotions, that isn't to say he's a pushover as he's every bit as sadistic as the others when the need calls for it.

Garrett ex-boxer once a professional now fights on the underground circuit. He's huge in size and the Enforcer of the group he also hates woman because of a traumatic past.

Finally, Diesel the torturer he's completely psychotic and definitely insane. He's one scary dude with a penchant for pain, blood and death he's also a bit of a pyro.

Each male here was so uniquely different all with such distinct personality traits. I loved how this built things up and was almost initially slow-burning in nature and the time that was taken with each connection here fully convincing me of the authenticity of the feelings involved.

Each connection has a slightly different flavour attached to it which only managed to showcase the whole individuality of this. I did have a favourite though, I adored Diesel and every time he called Roxy Little Bird I melted.
His extremely affectionate and bold personality with his little bird when he wasn't getting down and freaky helped to offset his more extreme sexual proclivities helping to Showcase a much more human side to him, at least with his little bird. Diesel got Roxy right from the onset his eccentric madness almost stripping away at the usual artifice.

So Den Of Vipers was intensely erotic and incredibly graphic in places. Its offset by the brilliant characterisation which makes this so much more than just some hot words on paper. I felt all this deep in my soul and believed in the portrayed dynamic of all the characters involved.

I loved the sheer extremities of the relationships here and all the over the top overt possessiveness. This was violent and uncompromising and such a major page-turner.
Be aware this really is graphic when it comes to described torture and such but that for me was part of the whole appeal here. Can't recommend this highly enough it was brilliant and also a really decent length as well. I literally binge read this I was that invested, one of my stand out reads this year and just maybe one of my favourite reverse-harem reads ever.
